macro.regime: Risk-on confirmed post-Nvidia, but Warsh's untested Jackson Hole debut tonight is the last coin flip before September
macro.narrative: Thursday 27 Aug's complete US close ratified Wednesday's Nvidia beat-and-raise: S&P 500 +0.72% to 7,730.99, Nasdaq +1.57% to 26,541, Russell 2000 +0.28% to 3,014, and VIX fell a sharp 4.6% to 14.51 -- the cleanest one-day confirmation yet that the AI-capex cycle and broad risk appetite are intact. Labor and growth data reinforced the soft-landing case: initial jobless claims fell to 203K (vs 208K consensus, a second straight weekly decline), and Wednesday's Core PCE (0.2% m/m, 3.3% y/y, in line) and Q2 GDP (confirmed at 1.5%, unchanged from the advance estimate, still a deceleration from Q1's 2.1%) neither re-accelerated inflation nor derailed growth -- Fed funds futures now sit split between a September hold and a residual ~30% hike probability, with essentially zero 2026 rate cuts priced. Commodities diverged: silver's real ETF (SLV) rallied 1.92% to $62.77 and gold's ETF (GLD) firmed a more modest 0.30% to $422.60 (the GC=F/SI=F futures headlines of +1.37%/+3.23% are thin, low-trust series this run and overstate the real move), while oil's ETF proxy (USO) jumped 2.09% to $130.01 even as energy equities (XLE) actually slipped 0.22% and the Iran-Oman Hormuz shipping-corridor talks remain in a 'final drafting stage' rather than a concluded deal. The 30-year Treasury still trades near a 22-year yield high (~5.27-5.33%) and the 10-year sits near 4.65%, keeping fiscal/duration stress alive even as HY credit spreads stay historically tight (~269-275bp OAS) -- a genuine divergence the market has not resolved. The dominant catalyst is now hours away: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote (Fri 28 Aug, 22:00 SGT / 10:00am ET), which he has previewed as focused on 'long-term structural questions' rather than near-term guidance, with the full Symposium ('Financial Innovation: Payments and Policy') opening the next day and Tokyo Core CPI (due 07:30 SGT, cons 1.8% vs prev 1.9%) the first data point of the Asia session.
